initiatives.name: Probe Gold Inc. Acquisition
initiatives.summary: Fresnillo completed the acquisition of Probe Gold Inc., a Canadian exploration company focused on gold properties, for all-cash consideration of CAD$3.65 per share. The transaction expands Fresnillo's presence into Canada and bolsters its exploration pipeline, particularly advancing the Novador project.

evidence.title: Acquisition of Probe Gold Inc for CAD$770 million
evidence.summary: Fresnillo completed the acquisition of Probe Gold Inc., a Canadian exploration company focused on gold properties, for all-cash consideration of CAD$3.65 per share. The transaction expands Fresnillo's presence into Canada and bolsters its exploration pipeline, particularly advancing the Novador project.
evidence.quote: Following extensive due diligence to ensure it had the potential to add considerable long- term value for our shareholders, we concluded the deal in January 2026 for an all-cash consideration of CAD$3.65 per share. The total equity value of the transaction was approximately CAD$770 million (approx. US$555 million) on a fully diluted basis.

initiatives.name: Silverstream Agreement Termination
initiatives.summary: The Board decided to terminate the Silverstream contract via a buy-back following a comprehensive review of ongoing operational and financial issues at the Sabinas mine. This resulted in a US$132.4 million net loss after taxes but was deemed in the best interests of shareholders.

evidence.title: Termination of Silverstream Agreement
evidence.summary: The Board decided to terminate the Silverstream contract via a buy-back following a comprehensive review of ongoing operational and financial issues at the Sabinas mine. This resulted in a US$132.4 million net loss after taxes but was deemed in the best interests of shareholders.
evidence.quote: As reported in the 2025 Interim Report, following a thorough evaluation of strategic options, it was concluded that terminating the Silverstream contract via a buy-back was in the best interests of Fresnillo and its shareholders. This resulted in a US$132.4 million net loss after taxes in the income statement, including the impacts of amortisation.

initiatives.name: Cost Reduction Through Contractor Optimization
initiatives.summary: Implementation of cost reduction initiatives including optimising the contractor base and decreasing maintenance and personnel costs. This resulted in a 6.0% decrease in cost per tonne and 17.7% reduction in all-in sustaining costs.

evidence.title: Cost Reduction Through Contractor Optimization
evidence.summary: Implementation of cost reduction initiatives including optimising the contractor base and decreasing maintenance and personnel costs. This resulted in a 6.0% decrease in cost per tonne and 17.7% reduction in all-in sustaining costs.
evidence.quote: In 2024, we continued to focus on cost reduction initiatives such as optimising the contractor base and decreasing maintenance and personnel costs. Cost per tonne decreased 6.0% to US$133.0, mainly driven by the reduction in the use of development and infrastructure contractors.

initiatives.name: Renewable Energy Target 2030
initiatives.summary: Fresnillo continues to target sourcing at least 75% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030, a target already surpassed since 2024. In 2025, renewable sources accounted for 77.8% of total electricity consumption, though this was slightly down from the previous period due to adverse climatic conditions.

evidence.title: Renewable energy target maintained at 75% by 2030
evidence.summary: Fresnillo continues to target sourcing at least 75% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030, a target already surpassed since 2024. In 2025, renewable sources accounted for 77.8% of total electricity consumption, though this was slightly down from the previous period due to adverse climatic conditions.
evidence.quote: Our target is to source at least 75% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030, an objective that has been surpassed since 2024. This target will remain unchanged, as new expansion and exploration projects continue to come online and place additional demand on available renewable capacity.

initiatives.name: Ciénega Water Treatment Project
initiatives.summary: Launch of a project to replace mine water with treated wastewater for mine auxiliary services, with treated water also used for irrigation. This initiative aims to avoid residual treated wastewater discharges.

evidence.title: Ciénega Water Treatment Project Launch
evidence.summary: Launch of a project to replace mine water with treated wastewater for mine auxiliary services, with treated water also used for irrigation. This initiative aims to avoid residual treated wastewater discharges.
evidence.quote: The year also saw the launch of a project in Ciénega to replace mine water with treated wastewater for mine auxiliary services. Additionally, a portion of treated water will be used for irrigating green areas, and alfalfa and oat crops grown for deer at the Wildlife Conservation Management Unit (UMA). This will avoid residual treated wastewater discharges.

initiatives.name: Tailings Storage Facilities Investment Program
initiatives.summary: The company invested US$102.6 million in eight TSF projects during 2025 as part of its strategic shift toward multi-year tailings solutions. This represents a step-change from incremental extensions to strategic planning that prioritizes safety, compliance and operational continuity.

evidence.title: Tailings Storage Facilities investment program

evidence.quote: In 2025, we invested US$102.6 million in eight TSF projects. Our operations comprise six active tailings facilities, three facilities under care and maintenance, and two additional facilities currently under construction.

initiatives.name: Water Infrastructure Investment and National Water Plan
initiatives.summary: Investment in water infrastructure including rehabilitation of Fresnillo city's water potabilisation plant, now renamed the Proaño Potable Water Plant. Commitment to annual return of 300,000 m³ of water as part of the 2024-2030 National Water Plan.

evidence.title: Water Infrastructure Investment and National Water Plan
evidence.summary: Investment in water infrastructure including rehabilitation of Fresnillo city's water potabilisation plant, now renamed the Proaño Potable Water Plant. Commitment to annual return of 300,000 m³ of water as part of the 2024-2030 National Water Plan.
evidence.quote: In 2024, we strengthened our collaboration with the Federal Government by committing an annual return of 300,000 m³ of water as part of the 2024-2030 National Water Plan. This included investing US$2 million during the year – out of a total US$7 million – to rehabilitate Fresnillo city's water potabilisation plant, now renamed the Proaño Potable Water Plant.

initiatives.name: Cost Reduction and Operational Efficiency
initiatives.summary: The company implemented various cost reduction initiatives and operational efficiencies across the business during 2025, which contributed to decreased costs and improved gross profit margins. These efforts are expected to continue supporting future performance regardless of external factors.

evidence.title: Cost reduction and operational efficiency initiatives
evidence.summary: The company implemented various cost reduction initiatives and operational efficiencies across the business during 2025, which contributed to decreased costs and improved gross profit margins. These efforts are expected to continue supporting future performance regardless of external factors.
evidence.quote: Our performance and cost reduction initiatives continue at pace – and these will help to underpin future performance regardless of external factors. Gross profit increased 113.8% year-on-year to US$2,664.1 million, mainly driven by higher adjusted revenue and decreased costs, the latter primarily due to lower volumes processed at some of our operations, including at San Julián DOB following its closure, the devaluation of the average exchange rate between the Mexican peso and US dollar, and cost reduction initiatives and efficiencies.

initiatives.name: External Auditor Rotation to PwC
initiatives.summary: The company completed a tender process for external audit services and recommended PwC as the new external auditor for 2027, replacing Ernst & Young LLP who had served since 2008. Steve Dobson rotated off as lead partner during 2025 and was succeeded by Stephney Dallmann.

evidence.title: External auditor rotation and tender process
evidence.summary: The company completed a tender process for external audit services and recommended PwC as the new external auditor for 2027, replacing Ernst & Young LLP who had served since 2008. Steve Dobson rotated off as lead partner during 2025 and was succeeded by Stephney Dallmann.
evidence.quote: Steve Dobson, who has been the Company's lead partner since 2020, rotated off the Company's audit during the year. His successor, Stephney Dallmann, who had been identified and agreed with the Committee in 2024, commenced her role in 2025. The conclusion of this process was that the Committee recommended to the Board that PwC be proposed as the external auditor for the year ending 31 December 2027.

initiatives.name: Engineers in Training Programme
initiatives.summary: Fresnillo continued its cohort-based recruitment system including the Engineers in Training programme for residency graduates. The 2025 cohort comprised 208 individuals, with efforts to achieve more gender-balanced recruitment as part of their DEI strategy.
